$note: Frame-time budgets for aura-web/e2e/hud-frametime.spec.ts (the v2 shell since T-0611; before it, GLASS_HUD §8.3 rule 6 over the legacy 8-panel scene) and the core's own check in e2e/ds-core.spec.ts. A frame is one `AnimationFrame` on the renderer's main thread in the Chromium trace — script, style, layout and paint for one rendering update — over the shell driven through every scene, an approval card, the launcher, the palette, a full screen and a resize, three passes under one trace, the best pass gated, measured after a settle so shader warm-up is not counted. The gated number is the frame's CPU time (thread time of the main-thread tasks inside it), not its wall time: on the 4-core dev LXC beside two gradle builds wall p95 doubled while CPU p95 held, because the thread was descheduled, not busier. Both profiles carry the spec's own budget — p95 ≤ 16.7 ms, no frame over 50 ms — and the profile (`gpu`, or `swiftshader` when WEBGL_debug_renderer_info names SwiftShader, which is what the runner's headless Chromium has) is recorded in .verify/hud-frametime.json so a number is never quoted without it. Today's UI (2026-11-08, swiftshader, three passes of 696 frames): cpu p95 1.42–1.68 ms, max 17–22 ms, wall p95 6.7 ms; the core alone (ds-core, 251 frames) cpu p95 1.26 ms, max 5 ms. The legacy room measured cpu p95 8.0–9.9 ms, max 22–24 ms. The budgets were not loosened when the surface changed (T-0611). Tighten, never loosen, without a trace in the commit body. blur_layers_max is 0 since Reactor II (2026-09-06; the popup since DECISIONS 54). cls_during_travel_max is 0: the core travels on transform alone, so a scene change that shifted layout is a regression.
